blocking.title: G12 and make review miss a file moved out of the reviewed paths: git diff --name-only folds the deletion into a rename
blocking.evidence: Both staleness checks list changed paths with `git diff --name-only <reviewed> <HEAD>`, which detects renames by default (git 2.43 here, diff.renames unset) and then prints only the new path. A non-exempt file moved into artifacts/review/ therefore shows up only under the exempt prefix, and its deletion is never seen. Reproduced in a scratch clone of 15c4319: committed artifacts/review/latest.json (verdict SHIP, reviewed_commit 15c4319), then ran `git mv tests/test_gate_mutations.py artifacts/review/old_mutation_tests.py` and committed. `git diff --name-only` listed only artifacts/review/latest.json and artifacts/review/old_mutation_tests.py, while `git diff --name-status --no-renames` showed `D tests/test_gate_mutations.py`. `python3 tools/review.py` printed REVIEW: SHIP (rc 0), and ship_check.gate_g12 returned PASS 'REVIEW: SHIP for 15c4319f9c3f, 0 blocking', even though the gate mutation suite was gone from tests/. Section 10.1 step 8 of the brief lets the reviewed commit differ from HEAD only in the exempt paths, so G12 passes while its property is false. The package already passes --no-renames in its own history queries for this reason (src/halflife/integrity/__init__.py:143 and :166). Fix: add --no-renames to both diffs, with a mutation test that renames a file into an exempt path.

blocking.title: G12 passes while make review ends with REVIEW: INVALID, because G12 still re-implements make review
blocking.evidence: tools/review.py schema_problems rejects a review whose reviewer is not 'subagent' or 'headless', and then make review prints REVIEW: INVALID. gate_g12 never reads the reviewer field and still does not run make review. Reproduced in a scratch clone of 15c4319: committed artifacts/review/latest.json with reviewer 'main-session', verdict SHIP, blocking [], final_line 'REVIEW: SHIP', and reviewed_commit 15c4319. `python3 tools/review.py` printed "invalid: reviewer must be 'subagent' or 'headless'" and REVIEW: INVALID (rc 1). gate_g12 on the same clone returned PASS 'REVIEW: SHIP for 15c4319f9c3f, 0 blocking'. Section 6 defines G12 as 'The latest make review ends with REVIEW: SHIP'. This is new evidence in the class of the previous B1: the D-053 fix made only the exempt lists equal, and its test (tests/test_gate_mutations.py:3308) compares only EXEMPT_FILES and EXEMPT_PREFIXES. Fix: have G12 apply tools/review.py's schema_problems and staleness, or run tools/review.py in the clone and require REVIEW: SHIP as its last line, with a mutation test for an invalid reviewer.

blocking.title: G10 still passes when README.md and docs/REPORT.md embed a figure with fabricated numbers that is not under docs/figures/ as *.svg
blocking.evidence: report --check (stale_parts) compares only the figures the build generates and other files that match docs/figures/*.svg. claimcheck and freshness read only the Markdown, so no check ever opens an image embedded from any other path, or in any other format. Reproduced in a scratch clone of 15c4319: copied docs/figures/pilot.svg to docs/img/pilot-copy.svg, changed 'Rule broken, granite: 2' and 'Rule broken, qwen: 2' to 0, embedded the copy in README.md (above **Status.**) and in docs/REPORT.md (above section 6), and committed. Running the clone's own code: CLAIMCHECK: PASS 162 claim(s) in 2 document(s); FRESHNESS: PASS 4 derivation(s), 125 live claim(s); REPORT: CURRENT (rc 0). All three G10 targets pass while both documents show a figure with fabricated violation counts, and rule 1 covers figures. By the same code, a PNG, or a file in a subdirectory of docs/figures/, is never compared, although docs/ARTIFACTS.md and D-053 say report-check covers every figure under docs/figures/. The previous B3 is fixed for the two committed SVGs, which are current today. Fix: fail when README.md or docs/REPORT.md embeds an image that the build does not generate, and when docs/figures/ holds any file the build does not write.

non_blocking: README.md:49 states counts of outcomes in words: 'had a false positive' (1 in artifacts/e0/detector_validation_initial.json, which docs/REPORT.md:100 renders from claim e0.initial.fp), 'with no false alarms', and 'caught every seeded violation'. All three are correct today. These are quantifiers, not numerals, so this is not the previous B4, but claimcheck cannot see them and they would not follow a re-run of E0 (see the E0 item). Generate the sentence from the claims, as docs/REPORT.md:100 does.

docs/REPORT.md:84 (the B4 fix) says 'Every pinned candidate family was considered; the pilot table in section 5.3 shows which ran each pilot template'. That table, built from artifacts/pilot/family_choice.json, lists four families and no templates. It omits llama, the fifth pinned family in artifacts/models/pins.json, which ran no pilot session. D-042 (DECISIONS.md:200) says Phi and Llama are 'reported as not fully piloted', and after the fix the report no longer says that any pinned family never ran. Add llama to the generated table (0 sessions, not fully piloted) or state the omission with a generated count.

README.md:41 says the four kit parts (halflife-guard, halflife-pin, re-injection, the rule-preserving compaction prompt) each come 'with measured overhead'. artifacts/e4/overhead.json measures only halflife-guard and halflife-pin, as docs/MITIGATIONS.md:3 says.

No test runs G10 or report --check against a hand-edited figure. tests/test_report.py:260-278 covers a stale block only, and tests/test_gate_mutations.py test_g10_requires_the_generated_report_to_be_current checks only that gate_g10 asks for the report-check target. This review's B3 would have surfaced as a failing mutation test.

G11 trusts each artifact's self-declared 'confirmatory' flag (src/halflife/integrity/prereg.py:256-260), and G8/G9 (tools/ship_check.py:1476-1648) never require a preregistration link for E3/E4 even though designs/e3.yaml and designs/e4.yaml declare confirmatory: true. The run tool refuses confirmatory plans without --prereg (src/halflife/experiment.py:543-553), so this is defense in depth; consider deriving confirmatory status from the committed design.

Probes advance the main run's seed counter (src/halflife/agent.py:258-260, temperature 0.7), so main-run sampling depends on how many probes ran. Probe content never enters the main context, and probes run in every E1 condition, so there is no bias between arms, but 'never contaminate the main run' holds for content only; say so, or give probes their own seed stream.
G5 probe leakage is recomputed only from per-session leak flags the harness wrote (src/halflife/experiment.py:445). Main-run contexts are not banked, so leakage cannot be re-derived from artifacts/.

E0 detector validation (artifacts/e0/detector_validation.json, git_sha 26a388f, 2026-10-23) predates the subject-env sandbox change (f3db2ec) and the template test-run pattern change (D-036). The current instrument has not been re-validated by E0, and the new pytest pattern is covered only by bench verify; note it in the E1 preregistration or re-run E0.

docs/REPORT.md:75 reports a simulation result (the score test 'held its nominal level where a plain cluster-robust sandwich rejected too often') with no banked artifact cited. docs/REPORT.md:53 ('the forced indices first drawn fell after most sessions had ended') is a dry-run observation with no artifact. Bank and cite both, or mark them unbanked.

README.md:36 hand-types benchmark composition ('Thirty small synthetic Python projects', 'two or three rules', 'four types'), while docs/REPORT.md renders the template count as claim bench.templates. These are design facts, not results, but they can go stale unchecked, as the 2026-11-11 CORRECTIONS.md entry shows.

Probe-scorer keyword groups were tuned on dev-split answers that cover the held-out E4 templates' rules too (src/halflife/data/probe_answers.yaml, D-038). This is not leakage into E4 outcomes, but the held-out templates are not unseen by instrument tuning; state it in the E4 preregistration.

RQ1 asks for half-life per agent, model, and constraint type. src/halflife/e1_analysis.py computes half-life per family only, and G7 checks it per family. Settle the per-type estimand (or its omission) in prereg/0001-e1.md.

make freshness accepts 'raw' primary artifacts on the strength of a self-reported provenance block (command and git_sha; src/halflife/integrity/freshness.py docstring). That is inherent offline, but docs/CLAIMS.md should say that raw-artifact authenticity is not verified.
artifacts/pilot/provenance.json records absolute build paths (/home/user/half-life/src/halflife/experiment.py ...). No secret is exposed; D-052 fixed this only for future runs.
